How to maximize your Social Security benefits, retirement savings

A couple thoughts about the topics covered in the article.

First on social security, while it is true the monthly payment will increase if you delay the age at which you start receiving payments, that may not be the best approach to maximize your payouts. It really depends on your life expectency. If your family has a history of living to 97 it is different than if the average is in the late-70s or early-80s. You need to take the different payments you would get by starting at different ages (first avaialable, available for full or 70), then apply them to the period you would expect to draw them based on your life expectancy, then discount those back to net present value. Waiting to draw social security until you are 70 could cost you money and you will never get back those years in your 60s when you could have received money and didn't.

Second on portfolio allocation, while it is generally agreed that one's mix of investments should grow more conservative as one approaches retirement, containing more safe bonds and less growth stocks, for instance. Once a person is in retirement, it is now the prevailing wisdom that one should begin to change the mix slowly back to a slightly more aggressive mix. After all, the further past retirement you get, the less money you will need because you are getting closer to death, but the more you may need to grow your assets for unexpected costs or unexpected inflation.
